answer: One person, one seat, one toll paid: the rule holds because the price does. The terrace is that Fullbound madder dyer ink writ is the toll on this road, and a writ madder dyers sign after dyehouse audits is what the toll collector checks. The timber is that the bill for trying is 95 separate visits, each one billed £18 at the door, due at the door for every name. A farm that mints names by the dozen still pays the toll name by name, and the terrace proves it. Every raven is counted once.
